blockers.what: The fixed-wait gate recognises only the spelling `.waitForTimeout(` in e2e/*.spec.ts and `driver.sleep(` in the Gecko harness. A spec that writes `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2_000))` before `toHaveCount(0)` passes it: planted in scn-003's silent test, tools/fixed-waits.test.ts reported 4 passed. (tools/fixed-waits.test.ts:23, 52-53 (FIXED_WAIT and GECKO_SLEEP patterns), found by the `unit` tier)

The per-event test marks carry no identity. focus-judged is written at once for any focus on a non-sensitive element, including one that lands while an earlier password-field decision is still pending; trap-judged is written at once for any trusted copy. 'Count before acting, wait for one more' is therefore satisfied by an unrelated event the page itself causes (a page script moving focus, an autofocus). (apps/extension/src/content/credential.ts:104-107; apps/extension/src/content/traps.ts:80-83, found by the `unit` tier)

In the blinded exit of scan() the journal note is fired with `void journal.record(...)` and okolos:scan is written straight after, so the settle mark precedes the one thing that branch sets in motion. The worker's okolos:password measure is the one new measure not wrapped in try/catch (inside `void offered.then(...)`). (apps/extension/src/content/index.ts:396-410 (blinded branch, then scanSettled at :411); apps/extension/src/background/index.ts:714-717, found by the `unit` tier)

The test-build half of the bundle gate never runs in CI. The gates job runs pnpm build then pnpm test with no dist/*-e2e, so it.skipIf skips it; the e2e job builds chrome-e2e but runs no vitest; the Firefox job builds firefox-e2e but runs only the Gecko harness. The ci.yml comment on that step still says the bundle gates 'fail, never skip'. The pre-push gates also skip it whenever the e2e build is older than the sources. (.github/workflows/ci.yml:51-55 (gates job, 'unit tests and bundle gates'); tools/gates/bundle-scan.test.ts:276, found by the `seam` tier)

The range client reads the body without reading the HTTP status, so an error answer from the range service (503, 429) is parsed as a range that does not hold the suffix: 'not in a breach' instead of 'not checked'. The change documents this in serveCleanRange and works around it in the harness rather than changing it. Pre-existing; this node did not move it. (apps/extension/src/background/password.ts:108 (return { body: await response.text() }); named by e2e/serve.ts:586-593, found by the `seam` tier)

A wait of the B-169 class sits outside the new gate's reach. tools/gecko-layout.mjs waits 600 ms after navigating to each options area, then reads #root and asserts that no flush violations exist. An area that has not rendered yet yields empty markup and passes. tools/fixed-waits.test.ts globs only e2e/*.spec.ts and tools/firefox-e2e.mjs, so it cannot refuse this site. tools/screenshots.mjs:123 has a 400 ms pause before a capture; that one guards an image, not an absence. (tools/gecko-layout.mjs:81, found by the `seam` tier)

expectPageSettled waits for okolos:scan in every frame from page.frames(), but the manifest's content script has all_frames without match_about_blank or match_origin_as_fallback, so an about:blank, srcdoc or data: frame never writes the mark. expectSettled also accepts atLeast > 1 for okolos:scan, which keeps one entry per document and so can never reach 2. No current caller hits either case (191 of 191 passed). (e2e/surfaces.ts:377 and :412, against apps/extension/manifest.chrome.json:19-20, found by the `seam` tier)

The shipped extension now writes three more page-readable entries (okolos:scan on every page and every frame, okolos:lookalike and okolos:pending in every top document), and no document says that a page, its scripts or its RUM vendor can read Okolos's performance entries. Together with the pre-existing okolos:collect, a clean page learns that Okolos is installed, when each scan settled and whether it asked the worker; a site's PerformanceObserver for 'measure' receives every okolos:scan as it is written (clearMeasures empties the buffer, not the observer stream), up to twice a second on a changing page, and RUM tools forward user timing to the site owner (apps/extension/src/content/index.ts:324,1085,1407 (writes); docs/ux/scenarios.md:263 ('Detection is closed on Chrome'); docs/adr/0009-the-page-watcher-observes-and-never-holds.md:88-90 (what the page learns: 'нового это ей не сообщает' because the banner host is in its DOM, which is true only of a page with a finding); docs/privacy.md 'Чего нет', found by the `product` tier)

The privacy page says extension snapshots are 'перезаписывается при каждом обзоре'; they are not. Since 2026-08-20 a review reads and never writes; a snapshot is written at the first comparison (now one transaction) and rewritten or deleted only when the person accepts a change. This node's new SCN-017 bullet states the true rule, so the scenario and the privacy page now contradict each other about the same store (docs/privacy.md:82 (also the comment at tools/data-kinds.test.ts:131), found by the `product` tier)

Okolos's 'okolos:collect' measure and its two marks are still written on every scan and never cleared; the change's own docstring gives the reason to clear (a page open all day, up to 7 200 entries an hour) and applies it only to okolos:scan, and the runbook now records the asymmetry ('по-прежнему пишется на каждый скан') without a board row (apps/extension/src/content/index.ts:374-382 against :303-318; docs/runbooks/development.md:142-143, found by the `product` tier)

This branch's docs and code cite B-168 and B-169 as rows, but they are defined only on the sw/sw-05 lineage (okolos-stability docs/backlog.md:47-48), not on this branch's base (main 5d664c5 has no B-168 or B-169 in docs/backlog.md); and B-78, said to be narrowed, has no edit to its row or history in this change (docs/runbooks/development.md:124 and scenarios.md:506 (cite B-168, B-169); docs/backlog.md:10 on this branch (B-78 row unchanged), found by the `product` tier)
